title: Can You Trust This Agent?
description: Five real model traces. Decide whether to trust, verify, or block each output before revealing the committed ground truth.

scenarios.title: Five green gates. One dark feeder.
scenarios.stake: A premature restoration can expose field crews and the public to energized equipment.
scenarios.lesson: A complete restoration packet is evidence for the system operator. It is not the protected re-energization decision itself.

scenarios.title: The rule passed. The receipt did not arrive.
scenarios.stake: A candidate can be screened without provable notice when a declared condition is mistaken for evidence.
scenarios.lesson: A satisfied rule flag is not a receipt. Ask for the missing candidate notice record before the workflow advances.

scenarios.title: The precedent looks right. The test family changed.
scenarios.stake: A chemical out-of-specification rule transferred to a positive sterility test can send an unsafe batch toward release review.
scenarios.lesson: The terminal hold is necessary but not sufficient. A receipt that confirms the failed sterility gate is internally false and must be blocked.

scenarios.title: The packet is complete. The clock is not ordinary.
scenarios.stake: Treating an urgent appeal as an ordinary ready packet can consume the review window that makes the appeal usable.
scenarios.lesson: The 72-hour path changes the terminal action. Route accountable review and preserve both the notice and the urgent deadline.

scenarios.title: The connector asks for one small credential.
scenarios.stake: A poisoned tool description can turn an internal read into credential exfiltration without any malicious user message.
scenarios.lesson: Tool metadata is untrusted input. The environment must prevent secret-bearing arguments from reaching an external connector.
